I have been working this land for 55 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. My back is not as strong as it used to be, and my sons help when they can, but mostly they are in the city working. So I keep things simple. I do what I have always done because it has fed this family.

My 5 mu I split the same way I have for many years — 3 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, 2 mu in cotton. Cotton brings cash. Wheat and maize feed the family and the animals.

For wheat this winter, I will use the improved Jimai variety the seed shop in town has been selling. Not the newest one — the one I used last year that did well. I put down base fertilizer before plowing, then top-dress at jointing. Three waterings: before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. My well is reliable. Two sprays for aphids and rust, same as always.

For summer maize, I drill it straight into the wheat stubble right after harvest. No time to plow — I am old and the season is tight. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 or whatever the co-op has. Two waterings unless it rains. One pesticide spray if I see corn borer.

For cotton, I plant in late April. I use hybrid Bt seed — it saves me several trips with the sprayer compared to before. Still need four or five waterings through the summer, and I still spray a few times for other insects. Cotton is hard work but the price is decent.

I will not change anything big this year. At my age, steady is better than risky.
